rationale:
Obligation: for a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, any arguments other than an object containing only `result` must end the request with `ValidationError::Agent`. Decoding the `result` value into `R` follows the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`. That requirement is context here and its tests are not reassessed.

Coverage:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#mod[submission_tests]/fn[submission_envelopes_require_one_result_field]` checks the envelope rule directly on `submitted_value`. It rejects every non-conforming shape and asserts the exact error message `submit_result requires exactly result`. The shapes are null, an array, a string, a bool, `{}`, an object with only a wrong key (`{"other":true}`), and an object with `result` plus an extra field. It also checks that a conforming `{result: X}` returns X unchanged for null, array, object and bool values. That covers the accept side of the boundary and the non-object, missing-field, wrong-field and extra-field classes.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[typed_submission_references_resolve_and_invalid_results_are_agent_errors]` checks the end-to-end outcome through `ValidationContext::ask`. It submits `{}`, `{"other":true}` and `{"result":true,"extra":true}` as arguments. Each ends in `Err(ValidationError::Agent(_))`, and the vetting callback panics if it is reached. This ties the envelope rejection to the required `ValidationError::Agent` error type. It also submits `{"result":"wrong"}`, which covers the cited decoding follow-through into `R`. A valid submission is also shown to succeed, and the advertised schema requires only `result` with `additionalProperties` false.

The non-object argument shapes are tested only at the `submitted_value` unit level. The end-to-end test shows that `submitted_value` rejections surface as `ValidationError::Agent`. Nothing in the text distinguishes non-object arguments from other invalid arguments in how the error is mapped. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. No unacknowledged gaps were found.
